title: Rainfall simulation and soil runoff
bodyMd:
Researchers investigated runoff using trays containing equal masses of the same dry soil. Each tray had the same area and drainage outlet. A rainfall simulator applied equal water volumes at a constant intensity. Runoff was collected for10min from the start of rain. Each result is the mean of four independently prepared trays randomly assigned to a treatment.

Experiment1 used bare soil and changed slope.

| Slope (degrees) | Runoff volume (mL) | Sediment mass in runoff (g) |
|---:|---:|---:|
|0|40|0.8|
|10|70|2.1|
|20|100|4.0|

Experiment2 held slope at10degrees and compared bare soil with soil covered by a uniform layer of plant litter. Rainfall conditions matched Experiment1.

| Surface | Runoff volume (mL) | Sediment mass in runoff (g) |
|---|---:|---:|
|Bare|70|2.1|
|Litter-covered|50|0.5|

Sediment concentration is sediment mass divided by runoff volume. The researchers measured no dissolved substances and did not test living plants, other soil types, or natural storms.
